### **Codex Entry: Faerûn, the Heartlands**

**Overview**
Faerûn is the vibrant, blood-soaked crown of the world of Toril. A sprawling continent of disparate cultures, it stretches from the frozen reaches of the Spine of the World to the humid jungles of Chult. To the scholar, it is a living library; to the adventurer, it is a crucible where legends are forged or extinguished.

**History: A Tapestry of Cataclysm**
The annals of Faerûn are defined by cycles of ascension and ruin. Its history began in the **Dawn Age**, a time of primordial giants and dragons. Most pivotal, however, was the fall of **Netheril**, an empire of mages whose hubris tore the sky asunder and shattered the Weave of magic. In more recent memory, the continent survived the **Spellplague** and the **Second Sundering**, celestial upheavals that reshaped the very geography and restored the gods to their distant domains.

**Significance**
Faerûn is the nexus of the Multiverse. It is here that the **Weave**—the raw fabric of magic overseen by the goddess Mystra—is most tangible. The continent serves as the primary battlefield for the eternal struggle between order and chaos. Its trade hubs, such as **Waterdeep** and **Baldur’s Gate**, dictate the economy of the Realms, while its ancient ruins hold artifacts capable of unmaking reality.

**Legends and Lore**
Common folk whisper of the **Time of Troubles**, when deities were forced to walk the earth as mortals, bleeding and dying in the streets. Tales endure of the **Chosen**, individuals touched by divine grace, and the mythical elven kingdom of **Myth Drannor**. Whether one seeks the forbidden secrets of **Candlekeep** or the gold of the **Zhentarim**, all paths in the Realms eventually lead to the Heartlands. 

*— Master Lorekeeper Alaric, 1492 DR*
